title: The withered fig tree and the fruit of the Spirit
english: On the withered fig tree. Mark adds that when Jesus saw a fig tree with leaves from a distance, he went to see whether he would find anything on it. Finding nothing but leaves only—for it was not the season for figs—he said, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again” (Mark 11:13-14). The fruit of the Spirit—love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, self-control (Galatians 5:22-23)—is sometimes produced in its proper seasons. But it is better if, even when circumstances press in the opposite direction against fruit-bearing, someone is able, because of being greatly helped by the word, to bear the fruits no less even then. And Jesus said to the disciples, “Ask for the great things, and the small things will be added to you; and ask for the heavenly things, and the earthly things will be added to you.”
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Origen is commenting on the Gospel account of Jesus cursing the fig tree, and he now explains the spiritual meaning of the tree's lack of fruit.

title: The authority of the Word revealed to fruit-bearers
english: After the entrance into the city and the casting out of those selling from the temple, the chief priests ask in what authority he does these things (Matthew 21:23). But he asks in return about the baptism of John, and exposes the hypocrisy of those unwilling to say whether it was from heaven or from men (Matthew 21:25). In this way the authority of the Word becomes clear to those bearing fruit, but is hidden from those having only leaves. Glory to Christ. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Origen is commenting on the events after Jesus enters the city and drives the sellers out of the temple, when the chief priests question his authority.
